newsitem.title: CANADA: Barrick proposes deal with Bre-X for Indonesian gold.
newsitem.headline: Barrick proposes deal with Bre-X for Indonesian gold.

text.p: Canadian gold giant Barrick Gold Corp. said Monday it had reached an agreement with Bre-X Minerals Ltd. to operate Indonesia's Busang deposit, one of the world's biggest gold finds.

Barrick and Bre-X Minerals, after weeks of uncertainty over whether a deal would be reached, have submitted a joint proposal to the Indonesian government to development Bre-X's huge gold discovery on the island of Borneo, Barrick said.
"The Government of Indonesia is expected to advise Barrick and Bre-X of its response in due course," Barrick said in a statement.
Indonesia's government advised Bre-X to make a deal with Barrick and extended the deadline for such an agreement to the end of December after a Dec. 4 deadline had passed.
The Busang property, in the Indonesian province of East Kalimantan, is estimated to contain at least 57 million ounces of gold, worth about $21 billion at current prices.

The Indonesian government wanted Bre-X, which discovered the gold, to take a 25 percent stake and Barrick a 75 percent share. It also suggested the two mining companies allocate 10 percent to the government.
The government's statements have angered Bre-X shareholders and hurt the company's once high-flying stock on Canadian stock exchanges.
The Barrick statement gave no other details. Barrick spokesman Vince Borg said the proposed deal followed the arrangement recommended by the Indonesian government.
"It's in accord with the government parameters," Borg said by telephone.
The tentative agreement will be finalised once the government gives the arrangement its blessing, Borg said, adding he did not know when that might happen.
He said he did not know if Bre-X shareholders would be required to vote on the proposal. Bre-X was expected to send out a statement later on Monday.
But Barrick's announcement did not calm worried Bre-X stockholders and other investors, analysts said.
"There are no details," said gold analyst John Ing with Maison Placements Canada Inc. "It is quite possible that they may not have a deal."
Bre-X officials did not return calls. The absence of a Bre-X statement so far was disturbing, analysts said.
